# CANDIDATE: VOLUME_WICK_REJECTION_AT_LEVEL

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis
At named levels (prior day high/low), a bar with long wick in the opposite direction of the break and below-average volume indicates rejection and reversal. This edge exists because low-volume wick rejection suggests lack of conviction in the break, leading to a reversal as liquidity is insufficient to sustain the move.

## Mechanism
Let level = prior day high (for short) or prior day low (for long). If price touches level (within 0.1% tolerance) AND bar has wick (shadow) opposite to touch that is >=60% of total bar range AND volume < 90% of average volume of last 20 bars, enter opposite to wick (e.g., long wick above level -> short) at bar close. Exit shape: Stop beyond the level (e.g., for short, stop above prior day high), TP at next named level or 1.0R. Regime hint: Effective during low-volume sessions (e.g., lunch 12:00-13:00 ET) and when VIX is moderate (15-25); avoid high-volume breakout days.
